assessments.evidence: Both present Joseph responding without retaliation. Genesis frames the sale as part of divine preservation, while Qur'an explicitly declares no reproach and invokes God's forgiveness.

dossier.title: Joseph's forgiveness and the recognition of Jacob
dossier.comparative_summary: Qur'an 12:91–95 portrays explicit confession, forgiveness, a shirt intended to restore Jacob's sight, and his recognition of Joseph's scent. Genesis 45 depicts Joseph's reassurance, family summons, wagons, gifts, and Jacob's eventual revival on hearing the news. Shirt-healing and scent recognition are not attested in this inspected Genesis chapter.
dossier.chronological_background: Genesis is a pre-Islamic scriptural tradition; literary formation, surviving Hebrew manuscript witnesses, Greek translation and Syriac transmission require distinct dating and independent research.
dossier.scholarly_interpretations: Shared narrative heritage and later exegetical developments remain hypotheses; no dependence conclusion is warranted.
